title: The incidence, risk factors, and consequences of Long/Post-COVID in people with diabetes compared to people without diabetes in Germany
summary: The main research question of this project is to gain detailed insights into the rates of new cases and the temporal trend of long/post COVID. An important goal is to identify risk factors for the development of long/post COVID in people with diabetes compared to people without diabetes and to validate them using machine learning methods. In addition, the long-term consequences of long/post-COVID will be investigated according to diabetes status: mortality, overall hospitalization rates and hospitalizations due to acute myocardial infarction, stroke, amputations and diabetic foot syndrome (DFS) within 12, 24 and 36 months after long/post-COVID.
conditions: The following ICD diagnoses for long/post-COVID are taken into account: U08.9, U09.9!, U10.9, G93.3 (only relevant for people with a previously diagnosed COVID-19). The analyses with an outpatient or inpatient COVID-19 diagnosis (ICD: U07.1) between 2020 and 2024 as a risk population are repeated.
Multisystem inflammatory syndrome associated with COVID-19, unspecified

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The study population for objective 1 is all SHI-insured persons between 2021 and 2024 (2021: 73.32 million; 2023: 74.31 million) who are stratified according to diabetes status (approx. 10% of all insured persons with diabetes).
The study population for objective 2 consists of all SHI-insured persons who will also be stratified by diabetes status between 2021 and 2023 according to the presence of a “long/post-COVID” diagnosis. The database is also to be expanded to include insured persons without a “long/post-COVID” diagnosis in order to estimate excess mortality and excess hospitalizations due to this diagnosis.
Exclusion criteria:
none, total survey Germany-wide
